experimental_procedure: Table 4, Entry 3: Reductive Alkylation of Methyl 5-Methoxy-3-[(trimethylsilyloxy)methyl)]benzoate (4) with Iodomethyl Pivalate. A mixture of 3.1 g (10 mmol) of ester 4 and 740 mg (10 mmol) of tert-butyl alcohol was placed in a dry 250 mL, three-necked round-bottom flask equipped with a magnetic stir bar, a coldfinger condenser topped with a nitrogen line, a low temperature thermometer, and a septum. The system was placed under a nitrogen atmosphere, and dry tetrahydrofuran (30 mL) was added via syringe. The septum was replaced with a gas inlet adapter attached to an ammonia tank. The coldfinger condenser was charged with dry ice−acetone, and the reaction flask was also cooled in a dry ice-acetone bath. Ammonia (100−120 mL) was condensed in the reaction vessel over a period of about 15 min, and then the gas inlet adapter was replaced with a glass stopper. The stirred solution was cooled to an internal temperature of −65 °C and 280 mg (40 mmol) of lithium metal was added (64 mg + 73 mg + 87 mg + 56 mg = 280 mg)) through the stoppered hole of the reaction flask over a period of 20 min. The solution maintained a deep blue color for 10 min after addition of the last piece of lithium. To the solution was added 4.84 g (20 mmol) of iodomethyl pivalate in one portion via pipet. The solution color changed from blue to yellow-orange. The mixture was stirred for 30 min at −65 °C, and 1.07 g (20 mmol) of solid ammonium chloride was added. The coldfinger condenser was quickly removed (after removing the nitrogen line), emptied, and returned to the reaction flask (without the nitrogen line), and the cold bath was removed. The stirred solution was allowed to warm to approximately −25 °C over a period of 25 min. A water bath was placed under the reaction flask and the reaction temperature increased to 20 °C over a period of 50 min. To the residue was added 60 mL of water followed by 150 mL of benzene. The phases were separated and the organic phase was dried (Na2SO4) and concentrated in vacuo (25−45 Torr at a temperature below 40 °C) to give 5.2 g of a pale yellow liquid. The residue was purified by chromatography over 120 g of flash silica gel (loaded and eluted with hexanes−ethyl acetate = 10:1) with collection of 50 mL fractions. Fractions 9−12 were pooled and concentrated in vacuo to give 2.83 g of 5a that solidified on standing. Fraction 13 gave 207 mg of a pale yellow liquid that gave a yellow solid on standing. NMR analysis indicated this material was a 4:3 molar ratio of 5a and 5b. 1H NMR spectra of the crude reaction product indicate a 7:1 molar ratio of 5a and 5b is produced in this reaction. 2.83 g (66%) of 5a as a colorless oil that solidified on standing, 4:3 molar ratio of 5a and 5b 5a: mp 54−58 °C; IR (neat) 1736, 1701, 1663 cm−1; 1H NMR (C6D6, 400 MHz) δ 0.0 (two s, 6H), 0.95 (s, 9H), 1.20 (s, 9H), 2.7 (s, 2H), 3.2 (s, 3H), 3.37 (s, 3H), 3.9 (s, 2H), 4.34 (d, J = 10 Hz, 1H), 4.5 (d, J = 10 Hz, 1H), 4.8 (s, 1H), 6.05 (s, 1H); 13C NMR (C6D6, 100 MHz) δ −5.4, 18.4, 25.9, 27.2, 29.6, 38.8, 51.3, 51.7, 53.8, 66.1, 70.0, 92.1, 119.3, 136.9, 156.1, 173.1, 177.1; exact mass calcd for C22H38O6Si (M + Na)+ m/z 449.2335, found m/z 449.2329. 5b: 1H NMR (C6D6) δ 1.16 (s, 9H), 1.45 (s, 3H), 2.48 (d, J = 22 Hz, 1H), 2.52 (d, J = 22 Hz, 1H), 3.22 (s, 3H), 3.36 (s, 3H), 4.37 (d, J = 10 Hz, 1H), 4.39 (d, J = 10 Hz, 1H), 4.82 (br s, 1H), 5.64 (m, 1H).

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Method A: (a) Ammonia (70 mL), was condensed into a heat gun dried, three-necked round-bottomed flask equipped with dry-ice condenser, mechanical stirrer and maintained at -78 °C, under a slight positive pressure of dry nitrogen, (b) A solution of an α -tetralone (1a-d, 16.4 mmol) in ether (8 mL) and tert-butanol (2 mL, 19 mmol), was introduced via a double needle and potassium (1.4 g; 36 mmol) was then added in small portions. After the addition was complete, the resulting blue suspension was stirred for 15 minutes, (c) To this suspension, anhydrous lithium bromide (3.14 g; 36 mmol)was then added and the mixture stirred vigorously for 30 minutes keeping the temperature at -78 °C. (d) Finally, an alkylating agent (methyl iodide, allyl bromide: 32 mmol) was added, and the mixture was stirred for 15 minutes. The cooling bath was removed, and the ammonia was allowed to evaporate. The residue was diluted with brine (40 mL) and ether (40 mL), the pH of the solution was adjusted to 7.5 by careful addition of cold 10 % HCl, the aqueous layer was then separated and extracted with more ether (4x25mL and EtOAc (4x 25 mL). reference: Birch Reductive Alkylation of Methyl m-(Hydroxymethyl)benzoate Derivatives and the Behavior of o- and p-(Hydroxymethyl)benzoates under Reductive Alkylation Conditions | Fretz, Samuel J.; Hadad, Christopher M.; Hart, David J.; Vyas, Shubham; Yang, Dexi | Journal of Organic Chemistry (2013), 78(1), 83-92
experimental_procedure: Table 4 Entries 1-2: Reductive alkylation of Methyl 5-Methoxy-3-(trimethylsilyloxymethyl) benzoate (4) with iodomethane. A mixture of 620 mg (2 mmol) of ester 4 and 148 mg (2 mmol) of tert-butyl alcohol was placed in a dry 100 mL 3-necked round bottom flask equipped with a magnetic stir bar, a cold finger condenser topped with a nitrogen line, a low temperature thermometer, and a septum. The system was placed under a nitrogen atmosphere and dry tetrahydrofuran (10 mL) was added via syringe. The septum was replaced with a gas inlet adapter attached to an ammonia tank. The cold finger condenser was charged with dry iceacetone and the reaction flask was also cooled in a dry ice-acetone bath. Ammonia (approximately 30 mL) was condensed in the reaction vessel over a period of about 10 min and then the gas inlet adapter was replaced with a glass stopper. The stirred solution was cooled to an internal temperature of -65 °C and 67 mg (9.5 mmol) of lithium metal was added in small pieces (32 mg + 10 mg + 10 mg + 10 mg + 5 mg = 67 mg), through the stoppered hole of the reaction flask, over a period of 40 min. The solution maintained a deep blue color for 10 min after addition of the last piece of lithium at which point 852 mg (6 mmol) of iodomethane was added via syringe through the stoppered hole of the reaction flask. The blue color dissipated after addition of the first 10 μL of halide after which the remaining halide was added in one portion. The mixture was stirred for 30 min at -65 °C and 267 mg (5 mmol) of solid ammonium chloride was added through the stoppered hole. The cold finger condenser was quickly removed (after removing the nitrogen line), emptied, and returned to the reaction flask (without the nitrogen line), and the cold bath was removed. The stirred solution was allowed to warm to approximately -28 °C over a period of 15 min. A water bath was placed under the reaction flask and the reaction temperature increased to 15 °C over a period of 30 min. To the residue was added 15 mL of water followed by 30 mL of benzene. The phases were separated and the organic phase was dried (Na2SO4) and concentrated in vacuo (25-45 torr at a temperature below 40 °C) to give 621 mg of a colorless liquid. The residue was purified by chromatography over 17 g of flash silica gel (loaded and eluted with hexanes-ethyl acetate = 20:1) with collection of 10 mL fractions. Fractions 9-15 were pooled and concentrated in vacuo to give 500 mg (76%) of 35 as a colorless oil. This material was contaminated with small amounts of compound 36 (7 mol %) based on 1H NMR spectroscopy. When the reaction was performed using 296 mg (4 mmol) of tert-butyl alcohol the product (35) (also contaminated with 36 as described above) was isolated in 61% yield. 500 mg (76%) of 35 as a colorless oil IR (neat) 1734 cm−1; 1H NMR (C6D6, 400 MHz) δ 0.0 (two s, 6H), 0.92 (s, 9H), 1.48 (s, 3H), 2.79 (br s, 2H), 3.22 (s, 3H), 3.33 (s, 3H), 3.92 (s, 2H), 4.81 (s, 1H), 5.90 (s, 1H); 13C NMR (C6D6, 100 MHz) δ −5.3, 18.4, 26.0, 28.4, 29.4, 46.6, 51.5, 53.7, 66.5, 97.0, 124.0, 134.4, 154.1, 175.6; exact mass calcd for C17H30O4Si (M + Na)+ m/z 349.1811, found m/z 349.1803.

A mixture of 2.80 g (10 mmol) of ester 9 and 0.74 g (10 mmol) of tert-butyl alcohol was placed in a dry 250 mL, three-necked round-bottom flask equipped with a magnetic stir bar, a cold finger condenser topped with a nitrogen line, a low temperature thermometer, and a septum. The system was placed under a nitrogen atmosphere and dry tetrahydrofuran (25 mL) was added via syringe. The septum wasre placed with a gas inlet adapter attached to an ammonia tank. Thecold finger condenser was charged with dry ice-acetone, and the reaction flask was cooled in a dry ice-acetone bath. Ammonia (approximately 100 mL) was condensed in the reaction vessel over aperiod of about 15 min, and then the gas inlet adapter was replaced with a glass stopper. The stirred solution was cooled to an internal temperature of −65 °C, and 167 mg (23.8 mmol) of lithium metal wasadded in small pieces (97 mg + 54 mg + 4 mg + 12 mg = 167 mg), through the stoppered hole of the reaction flask, over a period of 25 min. The solution maintained a deep blue color for 5 min after addition of the last piece of lithium at which point 4.26 g (30 mmol) of iodomethane was added via syringe through the stoppered hole of the reaction flask. The blue color dissipated after addition of the first few drops of iodomethane after which the remaining iodomethane was added in one portion. The mixture was stirred for 50 min at −67 °C,and 1.60 g (30 mmol) of solid ammonium chloride was added through the stoppered hole. The coldfinger condenser was quickly removed (after removing the nitrogen line), emptied, and returned to the reaction flask (without the nitrogen line), and the cold bath was removed. The stirred solution was allowed to warm to approximately −25 °C over a period of 25 min. A water bath was carefully placed under the reaction flask, and the reaction temperature increased to 22°C over a period of 80 min. To the residual solution containing white solid was added 40 mL of water followed by 80 mL of benzene. The phases were separated, and the organic phase was dried (Na2SO4) and concentrated in vacuo (25−45 Torr at a temperature below 40 °C) to give 2.92 g of residue. 1H NMR analysis indicated this material was mainly the desired product (29a) contaminated by 6 mol % of starting 9. The residue was purified by chromatography over 100 g of flash silica gel (loaded and eluted with hexanes−ethyl acetate = 9:1) with collection of 50 mL fractions. Fractions 5−9 were pooled and concentrated in vacuo to give 2.43 g of 29a as a colorless oil (contaminated with 6 mol % of 9 by 1H NMR). 2.43 g (82%) of 29a as a colorless oil IR (neat) 1735 cm−1; 1H NMR (C6D6, 400 MHz) δ 0.0 (s, 6H), 0.90 (s, 9H), 1.35 (s, 3H), 2.43 (br s, 2H), 3.28 (s, 3H), 3.90 (s, 2H), 5.14 (m, 1H), 5.8−6.0 (m, 2H); 13C NMR (C6D6, 100 MHz) δ −5.3, 18.4, 25.9, 26.6, 27.4, 44.9, 51.5, 66.9, 123.8, 124.0, 129.2, 134.1, 174.8; exact mass calcd for C16H28O3Si (M + Na)+ m/z 319.1705, found m/z 319.1701. The presence of 9 (6 mol %) was apparent from 1H NMR signals at δ −0.1, 3.45, and 4.45 and appropriate 13C NMR signals.

reference: Control of the Birch reduction of m-anisic acid to produce specific 3-oxocyclohexenecarboxylic acids | Webster, Francis X.; Silverstein, Robert M. | Synthesis (1987), (10), 922-4
experimental_procedure: 5-Oxo-1-cyclohexenecarboxylic Acid (8a): In a 2-liner, 3-nocked flask is placed m-anisic acid (3a: 50.0 g. 0.33 mol and H2O 75 mL). The flask is equipped with an efficient mechanical stirrer an ammonia inlet, and a cold-linger condenser containing solid carbon dioxide and acetone. Ammonia is admitted above the solution through a sintered glass filter; about 1 liter of ammonia is collected. The ammonia inlet is replaced with a nitrogen inlet, and a slow stream of nitrogen is introduced above the surface. Vigorous stirring is begun (caution: the solution may be super-heated), and lithium wire (7.0g, 10 mol) is added in small pieces over a period of 20- 30 min to carry out the Bitch reduction. Vigorous stirring is continued until the blue color completely disappears The stirring is stopped, the condenser is removed, and the ammonia is allowed to evaporate completely under a steady stream of nitrogen. Then a 1 normal potassium hydroxide solution (500 mL) (thoroughly purged with nitrogen) is added, and stirring is again started The solution is heated for 2.5 h with a water bath maintained at 60 °C. The water bath is replaced with an ice bath, and the solution is cooled to about 10 °C. With the ice bath still in place, concentrated HCl (100 mL) is added as quickly as possible without allowing the temperature to go over 70 °C. Stirring is continued until the solution temperature falls to about 15 °C. The ice bath is removed, and stirring, is continued until all of the solid is in solution. The aqueous solution is transferred to a 2-liter separatory funnel and extracted with (CH2Cl2 (3 x 200 mL). The combined organic extract is dried and evaporated on a rotary evaporator under reduced pressure. The crude product 8a is used for making the methyl ester. A sample of 8a is recrystallized from toluene. Yield 44.8 g, 96%. M.p. 99-100 °C. (Lit.7 m.p. 98-99 °C) 1H-NMR (CDCl3/TMS): δ = 2.25-2.88 (m, 4H); 3.17 (d, J =3 Hz, 2H); 7 33 (m, 1 H).

title: Birch reductions at room temperature with alkali metals in silica gel (Na2K-SG(I))
authors: Nandi, Partha; Dye, James L.; Jackson, James E.
reference: Birch reductions at room temperature with alkali metals in silica gel (Na2K-SG(I)) | Nandi, Partha; Dye, James L.; Jackson, James E. | Journal of Organic Chemistry (2009), 74(16), 5790-5792
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for M-SG Birch Reductions. In a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a glass-coated magnetic stir bar and a rubber septum, anthracene (178 mg, 1 mmol, 1 equiv) and Na2K-SG(I) (420 mg, 40% w/w original loading of metal alloy in silica gel; titrated reducing capacity 4.9 mmol electrons= 2.45 equiv40) were placed under an inert atmosphere (in a He drybox). To this flask was added 10 mL of anhydrous THF, and the mixture was stirred at room temperature for 6-8 h. The reaction color changed from colorless to dark blue. After this time, the reaction mixture was quenched with water (2 mL), added all at once. The resulting colorless mixture was then allowed to stir for 10 min. The organic layer was decanted, and the solid residues were washed with an additional 3x10 mL Et2O. After separation, the combined organics were passed through a Celite pad in a sintered glass funnel to afford a clear solution that was concentrated on a rotary evaporator. The product 9,10-dihydroanthracene was obtained as a white solid, yield 97%. Yield 86%. Information not present.
notes: solid-supported reagent, Birch reduction

authors: Sylvain, Catherine; Wagner, Alain; Mioskowski, Charles

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Birch Reduction; Typical Procedure: The aromatic compound (13.5 mmol) in MeOH (5 mL) was added to NH3 (45 mL) condensed at -80°C. Small pieces of sodium (78 mmol, 1.8 g) were then added. Once the sodium had disappeared (after a few minutes), Et2O (100 mL) and water (100 mL) were added. NH3 was cautiously removed under vacuum. The aqueous layer was then extracted with Et2O. The organic layers were dried (Na2SO4), filtered, and concentrated under vacuum. The crude material generally contained more than 95% of the desired product. Purifications were performed by rapid silica gel chromatography under N2 using a mixture of pentane and Et2O in the appropriate ratio as eluent. The final products were stored under argon at -20°C. 3-(4,7-Dihydrobenzo[1,3]dioxol-5-yl)propan-1-ol (2h), yield 35%. 1H NMR (CDCl3): δ = 1.3-1.5 (s, 1H, OH), 1.7 (tt, 2H, J = 8 Hz, J = 6.5 Hz, CCH2C), 2.2 (t, 2H, J = 8 Hz, CCH2C=), 2.9 (s, 4H, 2 x CH2C=), 3.7 (t, J = 6.5 Hz, 2H, CCH2O), 5.4-5.5 (m, 1H, CH=), 5.6 (s, 2H, OCH2O). 13C NMR (CDCl3): δ = 24.2, 26.9, 30.6, 33.3, 62.3, 98.0, 117.6, 131.2, 134.2. experimental_procedure: Cis-1-tert-butyl 2,5-dimethyl 2H-pyrrole-1,2,5(5H)-tricarboxylate (11) A solution of di-tert-butyl biphenyl (4.70 g, 17.7 mmol) in THF (250 mL) was cooled to 0°C under an atmosphere of argon. Lithium wire (2.50 g, 353 mmol), which had been washed in pentane and scraped with a scalpel to remove any oxide coating, was rapidly cut into small pieces (approx. 2 mm length) and dropped into the THF solution under an atmosphere of argon. After approximately 5 minutes a blue/green colour was observed. The LiDBB solution was stirred at 0°C for 3 hours before being cooled to −78°C. Pyrrole 3 (10.0 g, 35.3 mmol) in THF (150 mL) was added dropwise causing the blue colour to be replaced by a brown colour. The reaction mixture was stirred at −78°C for 16 hours. Di-tert-butyl phenol (29.1 g, 141 mmol) in THF (60 mL) was added dropwise and the reaction mixture was stirred at −78°C for 30 mins. Saturated ammonium chloride solution (50 mL) was added and the reaction vessel removed from the ice-bath. After 20 minutes the reaction mixture was poured into H2O (100 mL), via a Buchner funnel to remove any unreacted lithium wire, and the layers were separated. The aqueous layer was extracted with ethyl acetate (3 × 200 mL). The combined organic layers were then dried over MgSO4, filtered and the solvent was removed in vacuo. The crude product was purified by flash column chromatography [SiO2, diethyl ether-light petroleum (bp 40-60°C), 4:6] to afford a pale yellow oil (8.8 g, 88%) as a >10:1 mixture of diastereomers in favour of cis-dihydropyrrole 11. 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3) δH 5.93-5.85 (2H, m), 5.09-5.01 (2H, m), 3.75 (6H, s), 1.41 (9H, s); 13C NMR (100 MHz, CDCl3) δC 169.61, 169.15, 153.0, 127.6, 127.4, 81.1, 66.9, 66.6, 52.5, 52.4, 52.0, 28.2, 28.0, 27.9. experimental_procedure: D) General procedure for Birch reductive alkylation: In a dry three-necked flask equipped with a dry-ice condenser was introduced, under nitrogen, a biaryl (8 mmol) in THF (40 mL). In case the starting material is a phenol, n-BuLi (2.5M sol. in hexane, 1.1 eq.) was added dropwise at -78 °C and the solution was stirred for 10 minutes. The flask was then cooled to -78 °C and ammonia (approx. 80 mL) was condensed. Lithium wire (0.133 g, 19 mmol, 2.3 eq.) was added. The solution was stirred either at -78 °C for 30 minutes in case of "activated" biaryls (e.g. containing a 3,5-dimethoxyphenyl ring) or stirred at -33 °C (refluxing NH3) for 1h for the others. The red mixture was then cooled to -78 °C and chloroacetonitrile (1.6 mL, 24 mmol, 3 eq.) in THF (10 mL) was added in one portion (Methyl chloroacetate was added for 10a). The mixture turned immediately brown. After 5 minutes, ammonia was let to evaporate and a half-saturated aqueous ammonium chloride solution was added. title: Birch reductions at room temperature with alkali metals in silica gel (Na2K-SG(I))
authors: Nandi, Partha; Dye, James L.; Jackson, James E.
reference: Birch reductions at room temperature with alkali metals in silica gel (Na2K-SG(I)) | Nandi, Partha; Dye, James L.; Jackson, James E. | Journal of Organic Chemistry (2009), 74(16), 5790-5792
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for M-SG Birch Reductions. In a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a glass-coated magnetic stir bar and a rubber septum, anthracene (178 mg, 1 mmol, 1 equiv) and Na2K-SG(I) (420 mg, 40% w/w original loading of metal alloy in silica gel; titrated reducing capacity 4.9 mmol electrons= 2.45 equiv40) were placed under an inert atmosphere (in a He drybox). To this flask was added 10 mL of anhydrous THF, and the mixture was stirred at room temperature for 6-8 h. The reaction color changed from colorless to dark blue. After this time, the reaction mixture was quenched with water (2 mL), added all at once. The resulting colorless mixture was then allowed to stir for 10 min. The organic layer was decanted, and the solid residues were washed with an additional 3x10 mL Et2O. After separation, the combined organics were passed through a Celite pad in a sintered glass funnel to afford a clear solution that was concentrated on a rotary evaporator. The product 9,10-dihydroanthracene was obtained as a white solid, yield 97%. Yield 96%. Information not present.
notes: solid-supported reagent, Birch reduction

In case the starting material is a phenol, n-BuLi (2.5M sol. in hexane, 1.1 eq.) was added dropwise at -78 °C and the solution was stirred for 10 minutes. experimental_procedure: 1,4-Dihydoanisole 43. A three3-necked round-bottomed flask was fitted with a dry ice condenser and flame dried under vacuum. The flask was then cooled to -78 °C (acetone, dry ice) and ammonia (25 mL) was then distilled into the flask. Lithium (7.5 mmol, 52 mg) was added and once the metal had dissolved the carbamate 42 (70 mg, 0.15 mmol), in dry THF (2 mL) and EtOH (1 mL), was added slowly by syringe. Once the addition was complete, the syringe was rinsed with THF (1 mL) and this was then added to the flask. The temperature was then raised to -40 °C (acetone, dry ice) and the mixture was stirred for 3 h at this temperature. If the blue color dissipated during this time, then more small pieces of lithium were added. After 3 h MeOH (2 mL) was slowly added, and once the blue color had dissipated the ice bath was removed and the ammonia allowed to evaporate under a stream of argon. H2O (5 mL) was added, followed by Et2O (5 mL), and the organic layer was then washed with H2O and brine. The aqueous layers were re-extracted with EtOAc (2 x 5 mL), the combined organic layers were then dried over MgSO4 and filtered, and the solvent was removed under reduced pressure to give the crude 1,4- dihydroanisole 43 (70 mg, ~100%) as a white solid, which was used immediately in the next reaction. 1H NMR (300 MHz, CDCl3) key signals δ 4.86 (1H, br t, -NHCO2Me), 4.56 (1H, br t, H5), 3.65 (3H, s), 3.53 (3H, s), 3.08 (1H, 1H, dd, J = 5.1 Hz, J = 13.7 Hz), 0.93 (3H, s), 0.84 (9H, s), -0.002, -0.03 (6H, s).

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: D) General procedure for Birch reductive alkylation: In a dry three-necked flask equipped with a dry-ice condenser was introduced, under nitrogen, a biaryl (8 mmol) in THF (40 mL). The flask was then cooled to -78 °C and ammonia (approx. 80 mL) was condensed. Lithium wire (0.133 g, 19 mmol, 2.3 eq.) was added. authors: Gbara-Haj-Yahia, Isra; Zvilichovsky, Gury; Seri, Noa
reference: Ozonolysis of 1,4-Cyclohexadienes in the Presence of Methanol and Acid. Mechanism and Intermediates in the Conversion of 1,4-Cyclohexadiene Derivatives to β-Keto Esters | Gbara-Haj-Yahia, Isra; Zvilichovsky, Gury; Seri, Noa | Journal of Organic Chemistry (2004), 69(12), 4135-4139
experimental_procedure: 1. Improved Birch reduction of o, m, and p-Xylenes: When the procedure, which was described earlier1, was used, the yields of the dienes were low and were contaminated with major amounts of unchanged starting materials. The improved procedure was as follows: To 300 mL of liquid ammonia cooled on dry ice-acetone bath were slowly added: Ether (22 mL), t-butanol (120 mL) and 12.4 g (0.115 mole) of one of the xylenes. Lithium ribbon (6 g) was introduced in small pieces during 6 hours. The solution, which was blue during the addition, was left at -78º for additional 5 hrs. Most of the ammonia evaporated upon stirring overnight at room temperature. Water (100 mL) was added and the product extracted 3 times with petroleum ether (80 mL). The petroleum ether was dried on MgSO4 and evaporated in vacuum. The products (95% yield) were pure by NMR spectra, no traces of aromatic protons were observed. 1,4-dimethyl-1,4-cyclohexadiene 1H NMR (CDCl3): δ: 5.39 (br s, 2H, =CH), 2.55 (s, 4H, CH2), 1.66 (s, 6H, 2Me).
notes: Birch redn.
